stories.title: Fed Chair Warsh Gets Split Verdict on Latest CPI Reading
stories.summary: The latest CPI report is drawing sharply different reactions as Kevin Warsh's Fed weighs its next move. Former Fed economist Claudia Sahm reportedly called the data 'good news,' while Peter Schiff pushed back, calling the CPI rise 'misleading.' The divide underscores how contested the inflation picture remains heading into upcoming policy decisions.
stories.whyItMatters: How the Fed and prominent economists read inflation data directly shapes rate-path expectations, which move bond yields and equity valuations.
whatToWatch: Whether Warsh's Fed signals a shift in tone at its next meeting
Follow-up commentary from other Fed officials or economists on the CPI print
The next CPI release for confirmation or contradiction of either read
questions: What specific components of CPI are Sahm and Schiff disagreeing about?
Does this split reflect a broader divide inside the Fed itself?

sources.title: Kevin Warsh's Fed Faces Split Verdict on Inflation Data: Sahm Notes 'Good News,' Schiff Says Calls Out 'Misleading' CPI Rise

stories.title: An 800-Stock Active Fund Is Quietly Beating the Major Indexes
stories.summary: A broadly diversified active fund holding roughly 800 stocks is outperforming major market indexes, according to MarketWatch. The scale of holdings is unusual for an 'active' strategy, which typically implies concentrated, high-conviction bets rather than near-index-level breadth.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors have long debated active-versus-passive returns, and a fund this diversified beating benchmarks complicates the usual argument for either concentrated stock-picking or plain index investing.
whatToWatch: Whether the fund's outperformance persists over subsequent quarters

questions: What is actually driving the outperformance if the portfolio is this diversified?
